question: How long do created marshes take to reach biodiversity and function comparable to natural reference wetlands, and which attributes lag?
how_built: Claims from marsh, prairie-pothole, salt-marsh and constructed-wetland papers (ecosystem context plus a wetland word in the title). A claim is a comparison when its comparator is an undisturbed reference or its cause names the natural or reference site; its direction is turned into 'above_reference', 'comparable' or 'below_reference' for the created marsh. A claim whose cause is site age or time since restoration is a trajectory. Outcomes are pooled by outcome group.

short_answer.time_to_reference_note: No study in this corpus reports how long a created marsh takes to match a reference. The few time points come from chronosequences of restored prairie wetlands and are listed with each finding.

limitations: Thin evidence: 5 papers in all, most of them observational.
'Restored' and 'created' marshes are pooled; the corpus rarely says which, and drained-then-restored prairie potholes dominate.
A reference comparison at one age says nothing about the trajectory; do not read a lag at 4-6 years as a lag at 20.
Side reading is by keyword ('natural', 'reference' vs 'restored', 'reclaimed'): open the claims.
